correctness.rationale: For integral mu>0 and n>mu, Grau--Oller-Marcen--Sadornil Theorem 2(iv) gives n in S_mu iff mu/n+sum_{p|n}1/p is an integer. The only Omega(n)<=2 shapes are p,p^2,pq with p<q. In each case the positive numerator mu+1, mu+p, or mu+p+q is at most the corresponding denominator and strictly below twice it, so the integer is 1, giving mu=p-1, mu=p(p-1), or mu=pq-p-q, each with a direct converse. For mu=673: 674 composite, discriminant 1+4*673=2693 is between 51^2 and 52^2, and (p-1)(q-1)=674=2*337 has no pair giving distinct primes. This is an infinite theorem only within Omega<=2; the supplied small finite test is not its proof.
